extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists, photographers, video producers, editors and other editorial staff
extracted.subtask_description: Internal Reuters handbook of editorial standards covering legal/ethical rules, sourcing, conflicts of interest, image/video handling, captions, Photoshop rules, and procedures for complaints and incidents. Aimed at guiding newsroom behaviour and content production across text, photo and video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts, entertainment and inducements
rubrics_metrics.description: Such entertainment should not go beyond the bounds of normal, basic hospitality and needs to be in line with the Reuters policy on bribery, corruption, gifts and entertainment. Reuters does not use gifts of value, in cash or in kind, to influence sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must inform themselves of relevant restrictions before offering any gift and seek approval from their manager. Limited exceptions to prohibitions on payments/inducements apply only in very narrow circumstances (e.g. risk to life or facilitating small payments to speed legal/administrative processes). Such payments should generally be small, accurately recorded in expense reports and reported to managers and the Reuters Area General Counsel; on-the-spot decisions should still follow the spirit of guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence from commercial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not write stories, take photographs or film events to help clinch a sales contract or alter our coverage of a company, government or institution to suit Reuters commercial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply sound news judgment and produce stories/images that are accurate, fair and balanced. If a non-editorial colleague raises a reasoned complaint that something is unbalanced or incorrect, journalists have a duty to examine the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering competitions and accepting awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may submit journalistic work produced for Reuters for awards from reputable, disinterested sources only with manager approval; unsolicited awards and invitations to sit on juries need similar approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No Reuters work should be produced primarily for submission for an award or altered except to conform to competition rules. Approval will not be granted for awards from companies, lobby groups, governments, political parties or associations whose criteria are self-serving or could be construed as attempts to influence impartiality. Unsolicited awards should be reported to a manager for consideration; sympathetic treatment may be given to reputable media-rights groups or official institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and professional conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrity requires adherence to the highest ethical standards and the Reuters Trust Principles, accepting responsibilities and exhibiting a high degree of personal integrity at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When operating outside your home country respect local law, culture and custom. Always reveal conflicts of interest to a manager and protect privileged information and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legality of newsgathering
rubrics_metrics.description: We must ensure we are aware of and comply with laws, rules and standards in all countries where we operate; illicit methods (purloining data, breaking into premises, eavesdropping, taps, hacking, defeating passwords) must not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extremely rare public-interest cases that might require illegal actions must exhaust all legal means first and be decided at the highest editorial level in consultation with the Reuters General Counsel; see Legal Dangers section for fuller guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification as journalists / deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters journalists do not obtain news by deception. We identify ourselves at all times as working for Reuters and do not pass ourselves off as something other than a journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances where an assumption about who we are might be allowed in the interests of news-gathering should be governed by common sense and the spirit of the Code of Conduct. In all cases, staff must identify themselves as Reuters journalists if challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the same principles of sourcing, identification and verification online as in other forms of newsgathering; do not use internet material that is not sourced so it can be verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take the same precautions online as offline; consult the Handbook section 'Reporting from the Internet' for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading and tipping
rubrics_metrics.description: Insider trading is buying or selling securities while in possession of material, non-public information; tipping is improper disclosure. Reuters forbids staff to participate in insider trading or tipping information that could affect share prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat information obtained in employment as non-public until publicly disclosed and the market has time to absorb it. Material information examples: contemplated mergers, bankruptcy, business plans, government reports, forecasts, changes in management. Violations can be grounds for dismissal and are criminal in many jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationships with sources and conflict-of-interest avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources must be cultivated professionally; the basic rule is that we pay our own way. Maintain detachment from sources and avoid associations that might create a perception of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly spending substantial leisure time with a source may raise conflict concerns; ask whether you'd be comfortable spending equivalent time with sources on other sides. Disclose romantic or family attachments with news sources to a manager. Journalists should not report on or quote family members to avoid perceptions of favouritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with customers — editorial/commercial separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactions with customers (who may also be sources or subjects) should follow journalistic professional behaviours and maintain a clear line separating editorial and commercial functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be courteous and helpful but do not negotiate sales contracts; avoid misrepresenting to clients, defaming competitors, or encouraging clients to divulge competitors' confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting about people — sensitivity and harm minimization
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering people, avoid needless pain and offence, treat victims with sensitivity, eschew gossip about private lives of public figures, avoid sensationalism and seek clear, unambiguous accounts of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert for spin and bias (including your own). Apply integrity, impartiality, persistence, accountability and humility so that stories can be defended to sources and readers. See 'Reporting About People' for fuller guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with competitors — fair competition and limited cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compete vigorously to report the news first and best but compete fairly without placing obstacles in competitors' way. We should not do deals with competitors, trade material, or divulge editorial/corporate policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation is acceptable in limited circumstances (to reduce risk to life and limb, restricted access where pooling is in everyone's interest, staff safety, regulation, legal action to protect media rights). Attribute exclusive news obtained by competitors clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling complaints and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond promptly and properly to complaints about accuracy, balance or ethics; investigate promptly so corrective action can be taken if well founded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge complaints that cannot be immediately investigated, follow up quickly, handle at senior level in bureau/desk. Adopt constructive attitude; treat complaints as feedback. See 'Dealing with Complaints' for full procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to authorities' requests and protecting material
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for published or unpublished Reuters content from police, security forces, tribunals, lawyers or court participants should be referred to a senior editor who alerts the legal department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not voluntarily hand over published or unpublished material to authorities; consider lawful challenges to subpoenas. Distinguish between published and unpublished material and refer requests for published content to commercial services offering the material. Ship original tapes/picture files of sensitive situations to designated safekeeping locations as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal conduct, teamwork and reporting breaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Teamwork, joint planning and cooperation across disciplines (text, pictures, TV, graphics) is required; staff may contribute ideas and criticisms and have the right to a workplace free from harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share information, ideas and non-confidential contacts. Raise concerns about standards and ethics to managers without fear of recrimination. Treat all colleagues and associated individuals with dignity and respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident reporting and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal reporting of serious incidents (harm or risk to staff, significant problems with stories/images, hoaxes, allegations of improper behaviour) is essential and must be reported to supervisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must keep senior officials up to date, spot trends and take precautions. Non-managerial staff aware of incidents must report them to their supervisor. Familiarise with guidelines for dealing with threats and dangerous situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside activities and use of company resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must avoid confusion between professional activities and private interests; use of Reuters e-mail and communications for incidental personal use is permitted but expressions of political opinion or investment advice that identify Reuters breach the Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conduct private correspondence on company stationery or use identity cards to obtain special benefits not available to the public (exceptions: company-negotiated discounts or generally available journalists' discounts). Consult manager when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Always hold accuracy sacrosanct; images and stories must reflect reality and Reuters is transparent about errors, correcting them promptly and clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct errors openly in stories, captions, graphics or scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence is fundamental — avoid conflicts of interest or situations that create perceptions of conflict so Reuters can report impartially from all sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence stems from company structure and individual duty; reveal conflicts and seek managerial guidance when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values: Freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for balance and freedom from bias — neutral reporting is the Reuters hallmark and allows coverage of all sides without an agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for impartiality in selection, presentation and sourcing; guard against spin and personal bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values: Integrity (reiterated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the Reuters Trust Principles and acceptable professional standards in personal conduct; avoid fabrication and plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never fabricate or plagiarise; always reveal conflicts and respect privileged information and source protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photoshop and image-manipulation rules (permitted and prohibited)
rubrics_metrics.description: No additions or deletions to subject matter of original image; no excessive lightening/darkening/blurring; no excessive colour manipulation. Never alter a still or moving image beyond the requirements of normal image enhancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed: cropping, adjustment of levels to histogram limits, minor colour correction, sharpening (300%, radius 0.3, threshold 0), careful use of lasso, subtle use of burn tool, adjustment of highlights and shadows, eye dropper to check/set gray. Not allowed: additions/deletions, cloning & healing (except dust removal under strict limits), airbrush/paint, selective area sharpening, excessive lightening/darkening, excessive colour tone change, auto levels, blurring, eraser tool, quick mask, in-camera sharpening, in-camera saturation styles. Material alteration leads to dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photoshop technical and workflow guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Only minor Photoshop work should be performed in the field; photographers should rely on regional/global picture desks for further processing on calibrated hi-resolution screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use resolution set to 300 dpi; avoid auto levels; keep colour balance adjustments minimal; sharpen in Photoshop per settings above; cloning/healing only for sensor dust removal (below 100-pixel radius); third-party sharpening plug-ins not permitted; third-party noise-reduction plug-ins to be avoided unless approved by Chief Photographers. Camera settings: saturation/ image styles 'standard', in-camera sharpening OFF, Adobe RGB colour setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set-ups, staging and portrayal of images
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters photographers must not stage or re-enact news events, direct subjects or add/remove/move objects on a news assignment; news photography must depict reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers may direct subjects for portraits or non-news features but captions must not mislead readers into believing they are spontaneous. Composite images showing progression must indicate technique and are never acceptable in a news assignment. If media presence influences behaviour, captions must make that clear. Handout images must be examined for accuracy and reviewed by Duty Editor if suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption writing: accuracy, sourcing and tense
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions must adhere to Reuters rules of accuracy and freedom from bias and answer basic journalism questions: who, where, when, what, why. Captions are written in present tense, concise, simple English and generally a single sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a second sentence only if additional context is required. Contentious information (e.g. death tolls) must be sourced and explain circumstances and correct date. Captions must not contain photographer assumptions about what happened or what a person is thinking. Duty Editor-in-Charge will query incomplete captions; photographers must remain contactable until publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling images from controlled or escorted visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs taken under controlled conditions (organised or escorted visits) must state if the image was taken during an organised/escorted visit unless the photographer was truly free to work independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate circumstances in a short second sentence in the caption and consult Appendix 'A' of the Guide to Caption-Writing for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video sourcing and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Scripts and shot-lists must be clear as to the source of any video material used (Reuters, allied broadcaster, amateur video, third party with agenda).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify sources in script text (e.g., 'video provided by ...', 'video downloaded from a web site ...', 'amateur video obtained by Reuters ...'). Consult news editors before using third-party footage or photographs where copyright or authenticity may be an issue and provide additional information to clients about how coverage was gathered and the source of any video/textual information.
